key_finding: Talen's counterparty map is reshaping in 2024-2026 from a PJM merchant IPP into a long-term-contracted carbon-free baseload supplier to hyperscaler data centers. The single most consequential counterparty is Amazon (AWS) under the expanded June 2025 PPA — up to 1,920 MW carbon-free nuclear power through 2042. The reliability-must-run (RMR) contracts on Brandon Shores ($145M/year) and H.A. Wagner ($35M/year) plants provide an additional layer of contracted revenue stability through May 2029. PJM Interconnection remains the dominant wholesale market counterparty, with 8,745 MW cleared in the 2027/2028 capacity auction at $333.44/MW-day. Three pending or recently closed acquisitions (Freedom + Guernsey closed, Cornerstone agreed) bring additional gas-generation counterparties.

primary_customer_counterparties.name: Amazon Web Services / Amazon.com Inc.
primary_customer_counterparties.delivery_location: Susquehanna-adjacent Amazon data center campus + other Pennsylvania sites
primary_customer_counterparties.framing: Largest single carbon-free baseload data center PPA in US history. The PPA prices Susquehanna nuclear capacity at AI-workload-buyer rates significantly above the ~$27/MWh production cost — the spread is the structural economic improvement for Talen. The contract has a ramp schedule potentially reaching full 1,920 MW by 2032. Co-development of small modular reactors (SMRs) is a long-term option.

primary_customer_counterparties.name: PJM Interconnection (capacity market)
primary_customer_counterparties.type: Regional transmission organisation / wholesale capacity buyer
primary_customer_counterparties.framing: PJM's capacity auctions provide multi-year revenue visibility. The 2027/2028 clearing price of $333.44/MW-day on 8,745 MW of Talen capacity implies roughly $1.06B of annual capacity payments at that price level.

primary_customer_counterparties.name: PJM RMR Counterparties (Brandon Shores)
primary_customer_counterparties.framing: RMR contracts pay generators to keep otherwise-uneconomic plants available for grid reliability. Brandon Shores' $145M/year is among the largest RMR commitments in the PJM region.

fleet_acquisitions.name: Freedom and Guernsey
fleet_acquisitions.framing: Adds gas baseload capacity to complement the Susquehanna nuclear anchor. The combined gas fleet provides dispatchable capacity for periods when nuclear is constrained or when Amazon PPA delivery requires firming.

supply_chain_observations.fuel_uranium: Susquehanna nuclear fuel supply chain handled through long-term contracts with major fuel cycle suppliers — specifics not separately broken out in available filings at snapshot
supply_chain_observations.fuel_natural_gas: Pipeline gas supply for combined-cycle assets sourced through regional pipeline counterparties in the PJM region
supply_chain_observations.interconnection: Susquehanna and major gas assets interconnect directly to PJM transmission
supply_chain_observations.operations_and_maintenance: Talen operates its own nuclear and gas assets with internal O&M teams; some specialty services contracted to vendors

competitor_set_for_reference.name: Constellation Energy (CEG)
competitor_set_for_reference.framing: Largest US nuclear IPP; competing for hyperscaler data center PPAs. Director Joseph Nigro was previously CEO of Constellation.

competitor_set_for_reference.name: Vistra Corp (VST)
competitor_set_for_reference.framing: Texas-anchored IPP with growing nuclear and gas fleet; competing in PJM and ERCOT capacity markets.

competitor_set_for_reference.name: Dominion Energy (D)
competitor_set_for_reference.framing: Regulated utility with significant Virginia data center exposure; competing for Virginia hyperscaler PPAs.

competitor_set_for_reference.name: PSEG (PEG)
competitor_set_for_reference.framing: New Jersey utility with nuclear fleet; competes in PJM.

competitor_set_for_reference.name: Exelon (EXC)
competitor_set_for_reference.framing: Regulated utility holding company; Constellation Energy spun out 2022. Mac McFarland and Joseph Nigro have Exelon roots.

broader_ai_electricity_thesis: Talen sits at the intersection of two demand cycles: (a) hyperscaler AI data center power demand, which is growing at 25-40% annually in 2024-2026 in the PJM region; and (b) PJM capacity-market tightening, which is producing record clearing prices. The combination of (a) baseload nuclear capacity at low marginal cost, (b) gas capacity for dispatchable firming, and (c) RMR + capacity-market revenue layers makes Talen one of the cleanest pure-play AI electricity exposures available in the listed IPP universe.
